episodes.172614: A cluster of storms developed on the north side of the Twin Cities during the early evening of Tuesday, September 20th. These storms quickly became severe with a swath of very large hail, up to 3 inches in diameter, that fell between North St. Paul, Stillwater, Afton, and Woodbury.
episodes.172615: A cluster of storms that developed between the northern Twin Cities metro area, and  Amery in southern Polk County over west-central Wisconsin, quickly became severe with large hailstones falling across the area. The worst area that received up to 3 inch diameter hail occurred around River Falls. This storm tracked between Hudson and River Falls, southeast before moving into Buffalo and Trempealeau Counties. Although there wasn't any other reports of hail southeast of River Falls, based on radar and the track of the severe storm, very large hail likely fell between River Falls, Spring Valley, Eau Galle, Durand and Ellsworth. Other storms that became severe occurred between Menomonie, Eau Claire and Ladysmith, Wisconsin. There were pictures of cars damaged from the hailstone in River Falls.
episodes.172616: A southward-advancing cold front combined with unseasonably hot and humid conditions and marginal vertical wind shear late on the 21st to produce a broken line of strong thunderstorms across southern central Indiana.  Isolated downbursts produced wind damage in Rushville and portions of Decatur and Jennings Counties.
episodes.172769: A strong thunderstorm developed ahead of an approaching cold front during the overnight hours late Tuesday (9/20) into early Wednesday (9/21).  The storm produced large hail up to golf ball size as it traveled across central Wisconsin.
episodes.173188: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.173191: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.173217: A cold front brought marginally severe thunderstorms to portions of North Central Kansas during the evening hours of September 20th. The strongest activity occurred between 6-9 PM CDT, during which time a couple of marginally severe wind gusts were measured. No wind damage reports were received. Thunderstorms weakened considerably with loss of daytime heating during the late evening hours.
episodes.173505: Strong thunderstorms with a few embedded severe storms impacted southeast Michigan during the morning hours of September 21st.
episodes.173510: A thunderstorm moving through the Detroit River produced a wind gust to 35 knots.
episodes.173609: A thunderstorm dropped penny-sized hail just northwest of Big Bay in the early morning of the 21st.
episodes.173679: A strong shortwave punching into the Great Lakes provided support aloft for multiple clusters of thunderstorms to initiate in the presence of ample elevated instability on the morning of 9/21. These storms would go on to produce several severe hail reports across the southern portion of the CWA, including golf ball size hail in Gladwin county.
episodes.174051: A northward surge in tropical moisture will resulted widespread showers and thunderstorms across northern Arizona.  Heavy rain over far northcentral Arizona and south central Utah resulted in a flash flood. A strong rotating thunderstorms also developed over far eastern Arizona.
episodes.174121: Severe storms produced several reports of large hail of one to two inches in diameter as well as isolated pockets of damaging wind gusts in the form of downed trees and limbs.
episodes.174139: A deep upper level low coming ashore along the U.S. West Coast resulted in a combination of strong forcing, instability, and available moisture over the Salt Lake City forecast area. This event prompted an uncommon issuance of a Severe Thunderstorm Watch (number 541 of the year). Scattered strong wind gusts occurred, as did multiple instances of Flash Flooding.
episodes.174152: Scattered thunderstorms moved across part of western Wisconsin during the evening of September 20th. These storms produced large hail as they tracked from northern Buffalo County into Juneau County. The largest reported hail was up to three inches in diameter east of Finley (Juneau County).
episodes.174185: Several occurrences of severe thunderstorm wind gusts and flooding with heavy rain were reported on September 21st.
episodes.174206: High pressure across the southern Plains and low pressure across the Great Basin led to a southerly flow across the region, advecting deep moisture. PWATs rose to 2, which was near record for the period, and with the increased moisture instability values also rose with MLCAPE values in excess of 2,000 J/KG. The forcing from the aforementioned low pressure helped to enhance the thunderstorm activity as it was moving from south to north.
episodes.174289: A moist NE wind flow led to the formation of showers and thunderstorms over the near shore waters of Palm Beach County during the afternoon hours.
episodes.174552: A small area of gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with thunderstorms moving off the south Florida mainland and oceanside of Key Largo.
episodes.174584: Thunderstorms moved northeast across southeast Arizona from late morning into early evening. One storm produced damaging winds in Marana.

events.county: Jupiter Inlet To Deerfield Beach Fl Out 20Nm
events.narrative: Broadcast media relayed a report of a waterspout from a weak shower near Jupiter Beach. Time is estimated.

The Flood Control District of Maricopa County Gauge along Centennial Wash near the Railroad area reached action stage at 954 MST, with a peak flow of 10.12 feet (1341 cfs) at 1112 MST. Flash Flood impacts downstream where Centennial Wash crosses old U.S. 80 occurred 1.5 hours after action stage was reached, which is 6 miles downstream of the gauge. The flow returned below alarm stage at 1507 MST. No damages or injuries were reported.

Moderate rain moved over portions of Wire Pass and Buckskin Gulch slot canyons, as well as nearby drainages, with 1-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates up to 0.75 inches. Flash Flooding was reported by the Paria Contact Station at 12:00 pm MST, with reports of several hikers in the area needing to form human chains in three separate locations to escape flood waters. No injuries were noted at the time of report.
The Wig Mountain weather station recorded a wind gust of 59 mph as a result of a thunderstorm and its associated outflow winds moving over the site.
The Timmerman Hill ITD site measured a 59 mph thunderstorm outflow gust.

A strong thunderstorm moved through portions of the Paria River drainage basin, with widespread 1-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates of 0.50 to 0.75 inches. This generated a flood wave that propagated downstream, with the Paria near Kanab river gauge rising from 100 CFS around 1:00 pm MST to 1180 CFS at 1:25 pm MST.
The agrimet station RPTI1 recorded a 58 mph wind gust.

events.county: Hawk Channel From Ocean Reef To Craig Key Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A north wind gust of 41 knots was recorded at a WeatherFlow station at Carysfort Reef Light.

The Camel Back MTN weather station recorded an initial wind gust of 59 mph at 2:20 pm MST in association with nearby thunderstorm outflow winds. After a brief lull with lighter winds, an additional nearby shower resulted in more strong outflow winds which yielded a peak wind gust of 64 mph at 4:40 pm MST, and a final strong wind gust of 60 mph at 4:45 pm MST.

Thunderstorm downburst winds blew down trees through the town of Rushville and along the south side of town...damaging 6 homes, including partial roof damage to a building on the southwest side of Rushville.  Winds continued to down trees and powerlines to the southeast side of Rushville.
Thunderstorm downburst winds blew down trees and power lines in central Decatur County.

Strong thunderstorms moved over the Oquirrh Mountains over the course of an hour or two, resulting in moderate to at times heavy rain over the Jacob City Fire burn scar. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 1-hour rainfall estimates were in the 0.50 to 0.75 inch range. This was enough to result in a flow along Soldier Creek, which resulted in the evacuation of one house by State Route 36 and a road closure.
A 61 mph gust measured at the Dead Man Canyon FRD site.

A 68 mph wind gust measured at the ITD INL Puzzle site.

Thunderstorm downburst winds caused damage along Base Road from County Road 575 North to County Road 850 North, and to the northeast from that area.  Several large trees were uprooted while winds downed power lines, broke off power poles, and bent flagpoles to the ground.  Residences were impacted, as well as a plant farm where winds leveled a greenhouse and ripped plastic off of 2 others.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines on Sanders Rd. causing its closure and the lost of power for more than 2000 customers. Winds also downed several Palo Verde trees near  Moore Rd.

Multiple thunderstorms with moderate to heavy rainfall moved over Bryce Canyon National Park during the late evening hours. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor 3-hour rainfall estimates showed widespread amounts of 1 to 2 inches, and the Bryce Canyon Airport ASOS recorded nearly 1.5 inches of rain over the span of 3:30 pm MST to 4:30 pm MST. Many trails sustained damage, with some leading to extended trail closures. The Queen's Garden trail suffered a few debris flows with unstable footing and two retaining wall failures. The Peekaboo Loop suffered numerous debris flows and points of trail surface erosion. The Bryce Point Peekaboo Connecting Trail suffered numerous rockfalls and debris flows, two retaining wall failures, and deep incisions of around 1 foot into the trail surface. The Fairyland Loop trail suffered deep incisions of around 1 foot into the trail surface. The Navajo Loop trail had a tree downed on the Two Bridges side. The Wall Street side of the Navajo Loop Trail suffered further debris flows and complete trail erosion in some sections, resulting in an extended trail closure.
